---
indicator_code: "AMB-001"
indicator_name: "Ambulance Claims"
definition: |
  Tracks claims for **ambulance/EMS transport** from submission through to
  settlement. Every claim carries exactly one of **four pipeline statuses**:
  `UNDER_REVIEW`, `RETURNED`, `REJECTED`, `PAID`. **Submitted is not a fifth,
  independent status** — it is the total across all four, i.e. every claim
  that has ever been filed. The dashboard exists to reconcile the claims book
  (submitted vs paid vs rejected vs outstanding), surface the rejection rate
  by both count and value, monitor turnaround time from submission to
  adjudication, and show how long pending claims have been outstanding.

  > **Total Submitted = Paid + Rejected + Outstanding**
  > **Outstanding = Under Review + Returned**
  > **Total Submitted = Under Review + Returned + Rejected + Paid**

  This identity holds at every level of aggregation shown on the dashboard —
  the overall figure, and each vendor/county row.
numerator: |
  For the reconciliation identity: count and value of claims in each of the
  three legs (Paid / Rejected / Outstanding).

  For rejection rate: count and value of claims with status `REJECTED`.

  For TAT: `Adjudication Date − Submission Date`, for every claim that has
  reached a **terminal** decision (status `REJECTED` or `PAID`).
denominator: |
  - Reconciliation legs: **Total Submitted** (all claims regardless of status)
  - Rejection rate: **Total Submitted** (count and value)
  - TAT: claims with a terminal status (`REJECTED` or `PAID`) — excludes
    `UNDER_REVIEW` and `RETURNED`, neither of which has an adjudication date yet
unit_of_measure: |
  - **Count** — number of claims
  - **KES** — claim value
  - **Days** — TAT and ageing buckets (whole days, floor not rounded)
  - **%** — rejection rate (by count and by value) and aging bucket share
data_source: |
  - **Payor System** — claim submission, status, vendor, patient, county
  - **ERP** — payment confirmation (source of truth for `PAID` status)
frequency: "Real-time; values refresh on each page load."
disaggregation: |
  - Vendor (ambulance/EMS provider)
  - County
  - Claim Status (Submitted / Under Review / Returned / Rejected / Paid) —
    surfaced as a toggle on the Monthly Trend chart, not a global filter
  - Date Created
  - Date Incurred
filters: |
  - Created Date (month)
  - Incurred Date (month)
  - County (multi-select)
  - Vendor (multi-select)
acceptance_criteria: |
  - Total Submitted must always equal Paid + Rejected + Outstanding, for the
    overall figure and for every vendor/county rollup.
  - Both the Count and Amount card rows show all five labels (Submitted,
    Under Review, Returned, Rejected, Paid) — Submitted's value is always the
    sum of the other four, by construction.
  - Rejection rate is shown as **both** % of claim count and % of claim
    value — these are expected to diverge (a small number of high-value
    claims can move % of value independently of % of count).
  - TAT shows **both average and median**; median is the primary operational
    benchmark since a small number of stuck claims can inflate the average.
  - Ageing of pending (outstanding) claims can be toggled between **Created
    Date** and **Incurred Date** — this is a real recomputation of which
    bucket each claim falls into, not just a filter, since incurred date
    always precedes (or equals) created date and can materially change how
    old a claim looks.
  - The Monthly Trend chart carries a status toggle (Submitted / Under Review
    / Returned / Rejected / Paid) independent of the Created/Incurred date
    toggle — the two combine, so any of the five statuses can be viewed
    against either date field.
notes_caveats: |
  - **Submitted is a derived total, not a claim-level status.** No claim
    record ever has `status = SUBMITTED`; every filed claim is already at
    minimum `UNDER_REVIEW`. Submitted exists only as a KPI card / reporting
    concept equal to the sum of the four real statuses.
  - **Outstanding** = `UNDER_REVIEW` + `RETURNED`. These are the two "live"
    statuses still in SHA's processing pipeline — neither has reached a final
    decision.
  - `RETURNED` claims are sent back to the vendor pending further information
    and can re-enter the pipeline — they are not terminal, hence their
    inclusion in Outstanding rather than Rejected.
  - Ageing buckets: **0–7 / 8–30 / 31–60 / 60+ days** — deliberately more
    granular near-term than other claim-type ageing reports, since ambulance
    dispatch turnaround is expected to be fast.
  - Only claims with a terminal status (`REJECTED` or `PAID`) are included in
    the TAT calculation; claims still in `UNDER_REVIEW` or `RETURNED` have not
    yet reached a decision.
  - County-level figures reflect the vendor's operating county, not
    necessarily the patient's county of residence.
sdg_who_ref: |
  **SDG 3.8** — Universal Health Coverage; timely emergency transport
  reimbursement is a prerequisite for sustained ambulance service delivery.
---
